node-1.label: Recurrent diarrhea persisting for eight months following antibiotic treatment for aspiration pneumonia

node-2.label: The patient experienced more than 10 episodes of diarrhea daily, sometimes accompanied by blood and mucus; physical examination noted unformed stools with mucus occurring 5-6 times daily.

node-3.label: The patient is a 94-year-old man with medical history including chronic lymphocytic leukemia, aspiration pneumonia, reflux esophagitis, dysphagia requiring nasogastric tube feeding, sequelae of cerebral infarction with left hemiplegia, mild hypoproteinemia and anemia, prostate operation history with ongoing catheterization, and left eye blindness due to trauma.

why.why: Fecal PCR positivity for C. difficile toxin and colonoscopy erythema from ascending colon to rectum strongly support C. difficile infectious colitis; advanced age, CLL, and recent antibiotic exposure are consistent risk factors. However, pseudomembranes were not documented and biopsy/CMV testing are pending, so a concurrent CMV colitis cannot be fully excluded; confidence is set at 0.85.

PCR-confirmed C. difficile infection and the presence of bloody/mucoid stools make post-antibiotic gut dysbiosis unlikely as the primary cause; expert analyses support an infectious etiology. Confidence is reduced from 0.3 to 0.1.

Although blood and mucus initially raised concern for inflammatory/ischemic colitis, expert analysis notes that colonoscopy findings are more compatible with C. difficile infection and there is no pathological support for inflammatory/ischemic colitis. Ischemic colitis is a lesser consideration, so confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.1.

Enteral/medication diarrhea is unlikely to explain bloody/mucoid stools, and PCR-confirmed C. difficile infection plus expert assessment favoring infectious colitis further reduces its probability; confidence is lowered to 0.05.

node-8.label: Fecal PCR test is positive for Clostridium difficile toxin

node-9.label: Colonoscopy shows mucosal hyperemia/erythema from ascending colon to rectum

node-11.label: Biopsy pathology and CMV testing results are not yet available

node-12.label: CMV colitis as a concurrent or alternative infection

attrs.why: The patient's CLL-related immunosuppression and expert analyses indicating that CMV colitis or mixed infection cannot be excluded support considering CMV colitis. Colonoscopic erythema can also be seen in CMV colitis, but PCR positivity for C. difficile and the overall clinical picture favor C. difficile as the primary pathogen, so confidence is only 0.2.
